references.text: Isaiah 55:1 invites people to come to the water (God) to receive life, which mirrors Jesus' invitation in John 5:40 to come to Him for life.
Isaiah 53:1 describes that the message was not believed or received, paralleling how those in John 5:40 refuse to come to Jesus.
John 1:12 links the right to become God's children and receive life with receiving (coming to) Jesus, which is the theme of John 5:40.
In John 6:35, Jesus promises that whoever comes to Him will never hunger, a direct parallel to the promise of life through coming to Him in John 5:40.
John 7:37-38 repeats the invitation to come to Jesus for living water, a motif central to John 5:40.
John 12:46 emphasizes that Jesus came as light so that those who believe (come to Him) will not remain in darkness but have life.
John 14:6 confirms that Jesus is the way to the Father and to life, which is the core of the invitation in John 5:40.
